battle.name: 溫斯特魯特河戰役
battle.brief: 戰爭列表繫此役於 531 年，貝達《英格蘭人教會史》記在奧斯威在位第十三年、11 月 15 日，編年史另繫於 655 年。奧斯威在暴雨中的溫斯特魯特河擊敗彭達聯軍，彭達與東英格蘭王陣亡，三十名首領同死。卡面的羅馬重步兵不在陣中，它代表北方盾牆戰術與羅馬補給線的傳統來源。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 中世紀編年史把溫斯特魯特河戰役繫於七世紀中葉，具體是貝達《英格蘭人教會史》所記奧斯威「統治第十三年」的那一場；本站卡片沿用古代戰爭列表所列的 531 年繫年，這一出入必須先說明，以下寫的交戰方是依最接近的同名校戰役重建。北方是北寧王國：奧斯威以伯尼西亞為根據地即位，是梅瑟菲爾德戰死的奧斯瓦德之弟，他花了十三年間逐一收復德伊拉與北方教區，把王國重新統一在約克（Eboracum）這個羅馬舊都的周邊。奧斯威的軍隊由王室近衛、北方諸郡徵召的步兵，以及羅馬駐防線後裔的守軍組成，貝達形容其兵力「寡小」，人數遠少於對手，但訓練與士氣極高。南方與西方則是麥西亞王彭達的聯軍：麥西亞本身是英格蘭中部實力最強的政權，聯軍裡有東英格蘭王埃塞爾赫爾（Æthelhere）、圭內德領袖卡達法爾（Cadafael ap Cynfeddw），以及倒向麥西亞的德伊拉王埃塞爾瓦爾德（Æthelwald）。貝達說聯軍由「三十名戰首」率領，各氏族首領各領一支部伍，彭達居中號令。兩套指揮系統本質不同：麥西亞是王權加氏族首領的戰團聯盟，北方則更接近晚期羅馬行省軍制與王家常備軍的混合體，這一差別直接決定了戰役的走向。
countriesEn: Medieval chroniclers place the Battle of the Winwaed in the middle of the seventh century, specifically the engagement that Bede's Ecclesiastical History of the English People assigns to the thirteenth year of Oswiu's reign; this card follows the ancient list of battles, which files the war under the year 531, and that discrepancy has to be stated first, so the belligerents described below are reconstructed from the closest attested battle of the same name. On one side stood Northumbria: Oswiu, who had taken his throne in Bernicia and was the brother of Oswald, killed at Maserfield, and who spent thirteen years winning back Deira and the northern dioceses one by one, reuniting the kingdom around Eboracum, the old Roman capital. Oswiu's host was composed of the royal household war-band, foot levied from the northern shires, and the descendants of the garrisons left behind by Rome. Bede calls that force small in number, far fewer than its opponent, but its drill and its morale were excellent. On the other side stood the coalition of Penda of Mercia, whose kingdom was the strongest single power in the middle of England; to it were joined Æthelhere of East Anglia, the war-band of Gwynedd under Cadafael ap Cynfeddw, and Æthelwald of Deira, who had gone over to Mercia. Bede says the coalition was led by thirty war-dukes, each clan chief heading his own contingent while Penda gave orders from the middle. The two command systems were different in kind: Mercia was a war-band confederation of king and clan chiefs, whereas the northern army was closer to a mixture of late Roman provincial service and a royal standing force, and that difference decided the course of the battle.
people: 關鍵人物集中在兩位國王與一批各懷心思的盟友身上。奧斯威是這場戰役的實際策動者：他在北方被圍於「尤德城」（Urbis Iudeu，後人有指為斯特靈，亦有指為傑德堡）時，據說曾以大量財寶向彭達求和，並把幼子埃克格弗里思（Ecgfrith）交出作人質。傳記對彭達的回應說法不一，貝達稱他拒絕財寶、執意要自上而下摧毀奧斯威的部眾，《不列顛史》卻說彭達把財寶分給了威爾斯盟友。貝達另記奧斯威在戰前向上帝許願：若得勝，就讓女兒出家作修女，並捐出十二處莊園興建修院；戰後他把整場勝利說成神恩的見證。彭達是麥西亞的國王，也是當時唯一公開維持異教王權的英格蘭君主，親率大軍把北方逼到絕境，最終在敗亡中陣亡，屍首被斬下示眾。他的死直接改變了麥西亞的命運：北部歸奧斯威，南部由彭達的基督徒兒子佩達（Peada）統治，佩達又於 656 年被殺，繼位的伍爾赫雷與埃塞爾雷德則都是基督徒。戰場上還有兩位臨陣抽身的盟友：圭內德的卡達法爾帶兵離去，後世稱他「卡多梅德」，意即怯戰者；德伊拉的埃塞爾瓦爾德退到安全處等待結果。記錄此役的主要文獻作者是比德（Bede），十二世紀的亨廷登亨利（Henry of Huntingdon）又為它補上超自然的收場。
peopleEn: The decisive figures are two kings and a set of allies with divided loyalties. Oswiu was the man who actually drove the campaign: when he was shut up in the north at Urbs Iudeu, which later writers have variously identified with Stirling or with Jedburgh, he is said to have offered Penda a great deal of treasure in exchange for peace, and to have handed over his young son Ecgfrith as a hostage. The sources disagree about Penda's answer: Bede says he refused the treasure and was determined to destroy Oswiu's people from the highest to the lowest, while the Historia Brittonum says that Penda distributed the treasure among his British allies. Bede also records that before the battle Oswiu prayed to God and vowed, should he win, to make his daughter a nun and to grant twelve estates for the building of monasteries; afterwards he described the whole victory as the work of divine grace. Penda was the king of Mercia and the only English monarch at the time who openly maintained a pagan kingship; he led the host in person, drove the north to the brink, and was killed in his own defeat, his head cut off and displayed. His death changed the fate of Mercia directly: the north passed to Oswiu, the south to Penda's Christian son Peada, who was himself murdered in 656, after which Wulfhere and Æthelred ruled and both were Christians. Two allies stood apart from the fighting: Cadafael of Gwynedd led his men away before the battle, and later memory called him Cadomedd, the battle-shirker; and Æthelwald of Deira withdrew to a place of safety to await the outcome. The chief literary witness for the battle is Bede, and in the twelfth century Henry of Huntingdon added a supernatural ending to the story.
kits: 卡面上的羅馬重步兵並沒有出現在溫斯特魯特河的河灘上，這一點必須先講清：七世紀的英格蘭戰場上沒有任何一支羅馬軍團，北方與麥西亞的步兵用的是薩克森式裝備，即圓形或橢圓形的小盾、中央帶鐵乳突的盾心、木柄長矛（可投亦可刺）、短劍與斧；考古上可與之對照的是約克銅門街出土的七世紀鎖子甲片、與本特里格朗斯頭盔同類的鉚接式頭盔，以及羅瑟利寺與耶弗林王室遺址出土的投石索鉛彈，說明當時步兵的主要投射手段是投石索而非弓箭。卡面兵種在這場戰役裡的位置有兩層。第一層在戰術：羅馬重步兵的價值在於分段鎧甲與重盾所構成的密集盾牆，盎格魯—撒克遜戰術中同源的盾牆（þrythmo）就是這條血統的後裔，北方軍隊雖然人少，靠的正是把人擠在河岸與樹林之間的狹窄地帶、以盾牆頂住彭達大軍的正面衝擊。第二層在體制：羅馬重步兵的戰力從來不靠重裝，而靠補充兵源與補給線，這句話同樣適用於奧斯威，他的勝利靠的是十三年巡行所累積的據點、羅馬道路與河流渡口維持的補給，以及王權能夠把多支部隊沿同一條線調動的能力。卡面兵種與戰役的第三重關係在地理上，奧斯威的戰線沿羅馬不列顛的舊路北行，越過哈德良長城與北方要塞群，正是羅馬人留下的道路與駐防線，把溫斯特魯特河變成一次遠征可達的戰場。
kitsEn: The Roman legionary on the card never stood on the gravel banks of the Winwaed, and that has to be said plainly: there was no Roman army in the English field of battle in the seventh century. The infantry of both the north and of Mercia used Saxon equipment, namely small round or oval shields with an iron boss in the centre, wooden-shafted spears that could be thrown or thrust, short swords and axes. Archaeology offers the comparison: the seventh-century mail fragment from Coppergate in York, riveted helmets of the same family as the Benty Grange helmet, and lead sling bullets excavated at Rothley Temple and at the royal site of Yeavering, which show that the main missile weapon of the period's foot was the sling rather than the bow. The kit on the card therefore stands in this battle at two levels. The first is tactical: the value of the Roman legionary lay in the dense shield wall made of segmented armour and heavy shields, and the Anglo-Saxon shield wall (þrythmo) is the direct descendant of that tradition; the northern army, small in numbers, relied precisely on crowding its men into the narrow ground between the river bank and the woods and on holding the frontal charge of Penda's host behind a wall of shields. The second is institutional: the fighting power of a Roman legion never rested on heavy equipment but on the replacement of men and on the line of supply, and the same is true of Oswiu, whose victory rested on the posts accumulated over thirteen years of campaigning, on supply maintained along Roman roads and river crossings, and on a kingship able to move several contingents along the same line. The third sense in which the kit belongs to this campaign is geographical: Oswiu's line of march ran north along the old roads of Roman Britain, across Hadrian's Wall and the chain of northern forts, and it was the Roman roads and garrison stations that made a river like the Winwaed reachable by a distant expedition.
tactics: 彭達的戰術建立在三步之上：拉攏盟友、圍困北方君主、逼迫其接受條款。他集結東英格蘭、圭內德與德伊拉的部隊自南方北上，把奧斯威圍在北方要地「尤德城」，企圖以人質與財物換取奧斯威屈服；奧斯威交出財寶與幼子之後，聯軍開始回撤。戰役就在回撤途中爆發，貝達說兩軍在溫斯特魯特河相遇，交戰當日正下著大雨。北方軍隊的應對有兩個要點，一是利用河岸的狹窄地形與河道本身，把敵軍拉成沿河排列的縱隊，而不是讓它展開成橫陣；二是抓住聯軍的裂縫，圭內德軍在開戰前離去，德伊拉王退到安全處觀望，聯軍的攻勢在正面接觸之前就已鬆動。貝達記北方軍力寡小卻仍能取勝，說明地形與敵情比人數更關鍵。追擊階段同樣由水決定：麥西亞與東英格蘭的殘部在潰逃中被湧向河道與漫灘，貝達說淹死在逃跑中的人比死在刀下的更多，這句話既是戰況描述，也是這場戰役最典型的戰術特徵。戰後奧斯威沒有停在獲勝的地點，他把整次戰役帶到萊奧迪斯（Loidis，即今利茲一帶）的行政區才收束，說明這是長期戰役中的一個環節，而不是孤立的遭遇。
tacticsEn: Penda's tactics rested on three steps: to gather allies, to besiege the northern king, and to force him to accept terms. He collected the contingents of East Anglia, Gwynedd and Deira, marched north from the Midlands and shut Oswiu up in the northern stronghold called Urbs Iudeu, hoping to bring the king to terms through the hostage and the treasure; once Oswiu had handed over treasure and his son, the coalition began its march home. The battle broke out on that withdrawal, for Bede says the two armies met at the Winwaed on a day of heavy rain. The northern army's answer had two parts. First, it used the narrow ground along the bank and the river itself to pull the enemy into a column marching along the shore rather than letting it deploy into line. Second, it seized on the cracks in the coalition: the Gwynedd war-band left before the fighting began and the king of Deira withdrew to a safe place to watch, so the offensive had already gone slack before the lines even touched. Bede's remark that the northern force, though small, still won shows that ground and the state of the enemy mattered more than numbers. The pursuit too was decided by the water: the broken Mercian and East Anglian troops were driven in flight towards the channel and the flood plain, and Bede says that many more were drowned in the flight than destroyed by the sword, a remark that is both a description of the fighting and the most characteristic tactical feature of the battle. After the victory Oswiu did not stay where he had won; he carried the campaign on into the district of Loidis, around modern Leeds, before bringing it to a close, which shows that this was one episode of a long campaign rather than an isolated encounter.
data: 這場戰役站得住腳的數字不多，而且全部來自中世紀記載。戰役在貝達筆下繫於奧斯威在位第十三年，日期為 11 月 15 日；麥西亞聯軍由「三十名戰首」率領，而彭達、埃塞爾赫爾與三十名盟友首領同死；奧斯威所部被形容為人數寡小，具體數目無從得知。貝達另記逃亡中溺斃者多於戰死者，但只作比較，不給數目。奧斯威的許願留下可核對的份量：讓女兒出家，另捐十二處莊園興修院，莊園清單雖未保存，十二這個數目出自原文。戰役年分有兩套，盎格魯—撒克遜編年史把彭達之死記在 655 年，貝達的《英格蘭人教會史》把它歸在奧斯威在位第十三年，現代學者多據上下文取 655 年，另有學者依貝達文字次序主張實戰早於收束，可能早至 633 年甚至更早，本站卡片依古代戰爭列表採 531 年繫年，與上述中世紀記載皆不合，故此處的技術細節只能視為最接近的同名校戰役的重建。戰場位置同樣未定，那條河從未被確認，一說為今利茲一帶的科克貝克，一說為北唐卡斯特以北、匯入唐河的溫特河，2004 年安德魯·布里茲在《北方史》期刊上主張後者，現代研究給出的戰場位置在北緯 53.5 度一帶。
dataEn: Few numbers for this battle can be relied on, and all of them come from medieval accounts. Bede ties the battle to the thirteenth year of Oswiu's reign, to the date 15 November; the Mercian coalition was led by thirty war-dukes, and Penda, Æthelhere and those same thirty allied leaders were killed; Oswiu's force is described as small in numbers, and the actual figure is not recoverable. Bede adds that more were drowned in the flight than destroyed by the sword, but he gives only the comparison and no counts. Oswiu's vow leaves a checkable quantity: a daughter dedicated to religious life, and twelve estates granted for the building of monasteries; the list of the estates is lost, but the number twelve is in the original text. Two datings exist for the battle. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle enters Penda's death under 655, and Bede's Ecclesiastical History assigns the campaign to the thirteenth year of Oswiu's reign, so most modern scholars take 655 from the context, while others argue from the order of Bede's sentences that the battle itself came earlier, perhaps as early as 633 or even before. This card follows the ancient list of battles, which files the war under 531, a year that agrees with none of the medieval testimony, so every technical detail below must be read as a reconstruction of the closest attested battle of the same name. The position of the field is equally unsettled: the river has never been identified, one proposal being Cock Beck near modern Leeds and another the River Went north of Doncaster, which joins the Don; in 2004 Andrew Breeze argued for the latter in the journal Northern History, and modern work places the battlefield in the region of latitude 53.5 degrees north.
cause: 打起上嚟有三重原因疊在一起。第一重是北方的存亡：梅瑟菲爾德一役之後，德伊拉與伯尼西亞都臣服於麥西亞，北方王室只剩奧斯威一支人馬，而且被彭達逼到王國極北，連同本土教區都受威脅，奧斯威必須先贏回德伊拉，才談得上北寧王國。第二重是彭達的霸權：自 633 年哈特菲爾德追擊戰殺死埃德溫、642 年梅瑟菲爾德戰殺死奧斯瓦德，麥西亞已把勢力伸到英格蘭中部與東部，彭達還兩度進軍北方，甚至一度圍困班堡，企圖讓北寧永久屈服。第三重是宗教：彭達始終拒絕改宗，貝達因此把奧斯威的勝利寫成決定英格蘭宗教命運的結局，後世史家也把奧斯威的戰前許願讀成把軍事的復仇與教會的恩典綁在一起。此外還有一層私人因素，彭達扣住奧斯威的幼子作人質、拒絕歸還，等於把父子關係變成對方的抵押品，奧斯威寧可再打一場，也不接受以父子為籌碼的和約。直接的導火線則是聯軍回撤途中的一次遭遇，北方軍隊追擊彭達的縱隊，在河邊把對方截住。
causeEn: Three causes were stacked on top of one another. The first was the survival of the north: after Maserfield both Deira and Bernicia lay subject to Mercia, the northern royal house was reduced to Oswiu alone, and he was pressed back to the extreme north of the kingdom with his own dioceses under threat, so he had to win back Deira before there could be any question of Northumbria. The second was Penda's hegemony: since the battle at Hatfield Chase in 633, which killed Edwin, and Maserfield in 642, which killed Oswald, Mercia had extended its reach into the middle and the east of England, and Penda had campaigned north twice, at one point besieging Bamburgh, in the hope of bringing Northumbria permanently under his heel. The third cause was religious. Penda had never consented to conversion, so Bede made Oswiu's victory the hinge of the religious destiny of the English, and later historians read the vow made before the battle as the binding together of a military revenge and a favour of the church. There was a private strand as well: Penda held Oswiu's young son as a hostage and would not give him back, turning a father-son bond into the other side's pledge, and Oswiu preferred to fight again rather than accept a peace bought with his son. The immediate trigger was an encounter on the line of the coalition's withdrawal, when the northern army caught the Mercian column on the march and cut it off at the river.
impact: 這場戰役的直接後果是英格蘭霸權的一次翻轉。麥西亞自 633 年以來建立的霸主地位在一天之內崩塌，北寧的優勢重新恢復，但這次恢復並不長久，北寧對麥西亞的實際控制只維持了幾年，奧斯威在 678 年把王室駐地從約克移到切澤爾街一帶，說明北方自己也明白直接治理南方並不現實。麥西亞本身在戰後被分割，北部歸奧斯威直取，南部交給彭達的基督徒兒子佩達；佩達 656 年被殺，麥西亞先後由伍爾赫雷、埃塞爾雷德等王統治，而彭達死後麥西亞改宗，此後歷任麥西亞君主都是基督徒，北方教區與修道院網絡因而成為唯一貫通英格蘭的力量。宗教層面的影響更為深遠，1896 年查爾斯·普盧默就說此役對英格蘭的宗教命運具有決定性，盎格魯—撒克遜異教王權實際上在此終結。奧斯威的戰後捐贈也開始了北方的教會重建，657 年他與希爾達主持的惠特比會議成為英格蘭教會性質最終確立的關節。此外，戰役還在文獻中留下一個持續發酵的問題：戰場究竟在哪條河、這場戰役究竟發生在 633 年還是 655 年，十二世紀的亨廷登亨利甚至為它補上超自然干預的結局，使它由史事變成中世紀傳說的一部分。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the battle was a reversal of the balance of power in England. The supremacy Mercia had built since 633 collapsed in a single day and the primacy of Northumbria was restored, but the restoration did not last: Northumbrian authority over Mercia survived only a few years, and when Oswiu moved his royal seat from York to the vicinity of Chester-le-Street in 678 it was plain that the north too had grasped how impractical direct government of the south would be. Mercia itself was split after the battle, the north taken outright by Oswiu and the south handed over to Penda's Christian son Peada; Peada was murdered in 656, and Mercia was ruled afterwards by kings such as Wulfhere and Æthelred, every one of them a Christian, so that with Penda's death Mercia converted and the network of northern dioceses and monasteries became the one power running through the whole of England. The religious consequences ran deeper still. In 1896 Charles Plummer called the battle decisive as to the religious destiny of the English, and Anglo-Saxon pagan kingship effectively ended here. Oswiu's endowments after the victory began the rebuilding of the northern church, and the Synod of Whitby, held by him and Hilda in 657, fixed the character of the English church. The battle also left a question that has never stopped fermenting in the sources: which river was the field of battle, and whether the fight took place in 633 or 655. In the twelfth century Henry of Huntingdon even supplied a supernatural intervention, turning what had been a record of events into part of medieval legend.
result: 結果由貝達的敘述給出：北方得勝。彭達與東英格蘭王埃塞爾赫爾陣亡，屍首被斬下示眾，三十名盟友首領同死；圭內德的卡達法爾在開戰前帶兵離去，德伊拉的埃塞爾瓦爾德退到安全處，兩人的不出手成為麥西亞聯軍崩解的直接原因。麥西亞大軍在潰逃中被河道截住，貝達說淹死在逃跑中的人比死在刀下的更多，北方軍隊則在雨中完成了追擊。奧斯威把整次戰役收束於萊奧迪斯一帶，並以十二處莊園的捐贈兌現戰前的許願。政治上，麥西亞被切分，北方歸北寧、南部歸佩達，北方的優勢恢復但為期短暫；宗教上，彭達之死使英格蘭的異教王權實際告終。留下的空白與疑問同樣清楚：戰場的河流未能確認，雙方兵數無從核實，戰役的絕對年分在中世紀作家之間已有分歧，而本站沿用的 531 年繫年，更是晚出於所有中世紀記載的推斷，只能作為列表沿用的標記看待。
resultEn: The outcome is given by Bede: the north won. Penda and Æthelhere of East Anglia were killed, their heads cut off, and thirty allied leaders died with them; Cadafael of Gwynedd had led his men away before the fighting began and Æthelwald of Deira withdrew to a place of safety, and it was those two abstentions that directly broke up the Mercian coalition. The Mercian host was caught by the river in its flight, and Bede says that many more were drowned in the flight than destroyed by the sword, while the northern army completed the pursuit in the rain. Oswiu brought the campaign to a close in the district of Loidis and redeemed his vow of battle with the grant of twelve estates for the building of monasteries. Politically, Mercia was partitioned, the north to Northumbria and the south to Peada, and the northern advantage was restored but only for a short time; religiously, Penda's death brought Anglo-Saxon pagan kingship effectively to an end. The gaps and the uncertainties are just as clear: the river has never been identified, the numbers on both sides cannot be checked, the absolute date of the battle already divided medieval writers, and the year 531 used here is later than every medieval inference and can only be treated as a label carried over from the list.
